seo.title: New York City Homeless Help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified emergency shelter, food, health, employment, and other help for people experiencing homelessness in New York City.

content.text: Mental health or substance use crisis:

notice.text: Call ahead when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, appointment, service, job, benefit, or approval. If you have nowhere to sleep tonight, start with

content.text: If you have nowhere to sleep tonight:

go to the intake center that matches your household. City intake centers are open 24 hours a day, every day, including holidays. Applying at intake is the first step; the intake sites below are not the final shelter placement. Immigration status does not affect access, and interpreters are available.

Single adults are strongly encouraged to bring identification, but NYC says it is not required. Families should bring identification and documents for all household members if possible. Call 311 for directions or reasonable-accommodation information. The City does not provide transportation to intake.
DHS emergency-shelter intake for single men. This is an intake center, not a promise of a bed at this address.
both intake centers are open 24 hours, 7 days a week

items.name: Adult families with no children under 21

content.text: adult couples and qualifying adult family units with no children under 21. Bring identification and documents showing the family relationship.

items.name: Families with children under 21 and pregnant individuals

content.text: families with children under 21, single pregnant individuals, and families that include a pregnant person. All family members must be present. Bring household identification and relationship documents if possible.

items.name: The Bowery Mission — short-term overnight shelter

content.text: daily at 3 p.m. for women and 3:45 p.m. for men
up to 7 nights, meals, showers, clothing, case management, and referrals. Walk in or call. Space is limited; availability is not guaranteed.
breakfast at 8 a.m., lunch at 1 p.m., and dinner at 5:30 p.m., every day. No identification required.
a short Christian chapel service begins 30 minutes before each meal. Attendance is not required to receive food.
operated at the Episcopal Church of the Holy Apostles. The official service page does not state that worship is required for a meal.
The two religious organizations below provide practical help to anyone. Their faith identity is included so visitors can make an informed choice.
Christian, operated by Christian Herald Association.
free meals, showers, clothing, medical outreach, emergency shelter, case management, employment help, and pastoral care.
chapel precedes meals, but attendance is not required to receive a meal. Longer residential programs are faith-based; ask about program expectations before enrolling.
weekday soup kitchen and social-service assistance at 296 Ninth Avenue.
Official church website and worship information

showers, laundry, hot meals, clothing, case management, health connections, job help, and benefits help. Drop-in centers are open to everyone regardless of immigration status.
a drop-in center is not an overnight shelter with beds. Ask staff about current service timing when you arrive.

items.name: The Bowery Mission shower and clothing program

content.text: Monday, first 15 women; register at reception between 7 and 8 a.m.
Wednesday through Friday, first 20 men; line up outside between 6 and 6:30 a.m.
9:30 a.m. First come, first served. Hygiene items and clean clothing are provided as needed.
NYC drop-in centers provide clothing as part of their services. The

is a 24-hour Manhattan location. The Bowery Mission provides clean clothing through its limited, first-come shower program and a clothing closet for overnight guests. Availability and sizes can change; ask before traveling.

The Bowery Mission official help page

content.text: Call 911 for a medical emergency. For a mental health or substance use crisis, call or text 988.
primary care, mental health and substance use treatment, prescriptions, vaccinations, and other care through NYC Health + Hospitals.
sliding-scale fees can start at $0. The program is for New Yorkers who do not have health insurance and cannot afford private insurance, regardless of immigration status. Enrollment is not automatic.

items.name: The Bowery Mission mobile medical care

content.text: Tuesday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.; Thursday, 2 to 5 p.m.
free medical care through a Project Renewal mobile medical van, regardless of insurance status.
also provides health care at locations across the city; use its official “Find Care in NYC” directory for a current site.

Free or public restrooms are available in some parks, libraries, public spaces, and transit hubs. Hours and working status change. Use the City's official map and check the location details before traveling.

items.text: NYC DOT restroom locations and hours

content.text: free public internet and computer access at library locations in Manhattan, the Bronx, and Staten Island. Brooklyn and Queens have separate public-library systems.

use the official location finder for current hours. Ask branch staff about computer reservations, library-card requirements, power outlets, restrooms, and accessibility before relying on a specific branch.
People ages 14 through 24 can use city-funded youth drop-in centers for phone charging, food, clothing, showers, laundry, health connections, job support, and shelter referrals.
See official youth drop-in locations and hours
No general free-transit program for all adults experiencing homelessness was confirmed. These official programs may help:

items.text: eligible low-income residents ages 18 through 64 can receive 50% off subway, eligible bus, and Access-A-Ride fares. Immigration status does not affect eligibility. Call 311 or
eligible students can receive school transportation or an OMNY card; parents or guardians may receive a card to accompany a child. Ask the child's school or
read the official school transportation rules
people applying for shelter or already in shelter who have a confirmed housing option outside NYC may qualify for one-way bus, train, or air travel. Ask shelter or intake staff.

items.name: ACCESS HRA and Benefits Access Centers

content.text: Cash Assistance, SNAP food benefits, Medicaid for eligible groups, emergency grants, rental help, and other benefits.
online through ACCESS HRA or in person at an HRA Benefits Access Center. Requirements vary. Applying does not guarantee approval.
Bring whatever documents you have. If you lack identification or a permanent address, tell the worker and ask what alternative proof is accepted.

free one-to-one career help, job matching, recruitment events, résumé and interview workshops, job-search resources, and training referrals. Help is available online, by phone, and in person at centers across the five boroughs.

people age 18 or older who are legally authorized to work in the United States. ACCESS NYC also lists NYC residence as a requirement; ask Workforce1 how to document residence if you do not have a permanent address.

items.name: New York Public Library one-to-one job support

content.text: free appointments for help writing or formatting a résumé and cover letter, completing applications, finding job boards, and locating training or interview clothing.
in person or remotely by phone or Google Meet. Appointments open weekly and may fill.

items.name: The Bowery Mission residential employment support

content.text: job-search assistance, career coaching, résumé support, training, tutoring, and interview preparation for people accepted into its faith-based residential programs.
this is not a general walk-in job center. Ask about residential-program admission and expectations.

items.text: Ask a drop-in center, shelter, or case manager for help establishing a safe mailing contact. Never use an organization's address without permission.
Use a phone number and email account that you can check reliably. Public libraries offer computers and internet for applications.
Keep copies of your résumé, identification, work-authorization documents, applications, and employer responses when possible.
Tell Workforce1 or library staff which documents, phone access, interview clothing, or transportation you lack so they can identify appropriate referrals.
Check the official Jobs NYC events page shortly before attending; dates, registration rules, and locations change.

content.text: . For eviction or housing-court help, say “Tenant Helpline.”

free legal help may be available for eviction, housing, immigration, wage theft, employment, and other civil matters. You do not need to be an HRA client, and immigration status does not prevent access to the service.
eligibility and representation depend on the case. A lawyer working through the City's program will not ask you to pay.
free city photo identification for NYC residents age 10 and older.
If you have no stable address:

a City agency, nonprofit, religious institution, hospital, or health clinic can provide an official letter establishing NYC residency. The card can omit an address. An eligible organization may also permit its address to appear as a “care-of” address.
review the document guide and make an enrollment-center appointment. Approval depends on the documents accepted by IDNYC.

items.text: Documents and forms for applicants without a home address

content.text: For a birth certificate, Social Security card, state ID, or driver's license, ask a shelter or drop-in case manager about the correct issuing agency, accepted address proof, and possible fee assistance. Do not pay an unofficial service to obtain government documents.
free mail pickup at an authorized Post Office without a street address. Availability, identification rules, and how long mail is held depend on the facility.
contact the Post Office to confirm that it offers General Delivery and ask for the correct ZIP Code and pickup rules.
Some shelters, drop-in centers, nonprofits, and religious organizations may receive mail for active clients. Ask the organization first; never use its address without permission.
an allowance for storage of furniture and personal belongings may be available during temporary shelter, eviction, or relocation if the person qualifies for Cash Assistance or Emergency Assistance.
apply through ACCESS HRA, or ask an outreach team, shelter case manager, or HRA worker for help. Eligibility and size or cost limits apply.

items.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

content.text: free, confidential connection to VA homeless programs, health care, housing services, and local VA staff. Veterans, family, friends, and service providers may call.
call or text 911 if you are in immediate danger.

free, confidential support for domestic or intimate-partner violence, sexual violence, trafficking, stalking, elder abuse, and other crimes. Advocates can help with safety planning, shelter options, and referrals in multiple languages.
shelter addresses are confidential and are not published here. If an abuser may monitor your device, calling can be safer than browsing.

NYC DHS does not allow pets to live in shelter with clients. Service animals are permitted. Requests involving emotional support animals are considered individually. Do not surrender an animal before asking about prevention or temporary-care options.

items.name: Animal Care Centers of NYC and pet-support options

content.text: ACC counselors may be able to connect owners with resources intended to keep people and pets together, reduced-cost veterinary care, or placement options. Appointments are recommended for intake.
and tell the advocate that you need safety with a pet; some programs may allow survivors and pets to stay together.

content.text: Public-transit fares and service can change. Check the official MTA pages before traveling. For the correct shelter intake center after reaching the city, call 311.
take the AirTrain to Jamaica Station, then take the subway toward Manhattan. The MTA also lists an AirTrain connection at Howard Beach.
$11.75 for most riders: $8.75 AirTrain plus $3 subway. Unlimited passes do not cover AirTrain.
varies by terminal, wait time, destination, and overnight service; the MTA advises allowing extra time.
take the free Q70 bus to Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue or 74 Street-Broadway, then take the subway toward Manhattan. The M60 bus connects the airport with Upper Manhattan.
$3 for the subway plus free Q70 bus; the M60 costs $3 for most riders.
the MTA says the trip can take up to an hour or more depending on the route and traffic.

items.name: NYC homeless outreach and 24-hour drop-in centers

content.text: to request outreach for a person living on the street or subway. Call 911 for a medical emergency, immediate danger, or a person on subway tracks.

Drop-in centers offer a place to come indoors, hot meals, clothing, showers, laundry, case management, health connections, job help, and benefits help. All listed City centers are open 24 hours a day, every day. They are not shelters with beds.
call 311 or ask a drop-in center about current warming or cooling locations. During a City Code Blue, additional open-door rules apply at shelters, drop-in centers, and designated hospitals.
